cohort: The study included 79 women with primary adrenal insufficiency (PAI) who had a total of 101 pregnancies.
finding: The study found that women with PAI experienced a high rate of adrenal crisis during pregnancy (18.8% of pregnancies), and had higher rates of caesarean birth (63.9%) and prematurity (21.2%) compared to the UK average, despite generally favourable obstetric outcomes.
mod_finding: The caesarean section rate for women with PAI was 63.9%, which was higher than the UK average.
